I farm only 3.0 mu, so I will keep the whole area in stevia this year instead of splitting land or trying another crop. With such a small plot, I care more about stable management and clean field work than taking big risks. I have 20 years of farming experience, and since some people in my household work off-farm, I will choose a practical plan that I can manage on time without needing too much extra labor. I have well irrigation, so I will rely on that to keep moisture steady after establishment and during the stronger growth period. I will use improved seed material because I want more uniform plants and steadier output than older traditional stock. For fertilization, I will use a moderate program: enough nitrogen to push vegetative growth, but not so much that the crop becomes too soft; phosphorus for rooting and establishment; potassium to support leaf yield and plant strength. I will do rotary tillage because it is efficient for my small area and gives me a workable seedbed without the heavier effort of ploughing. I will keep pesticide use limited and only plan a few sprays, because I want to control problems but avoid unnecessary cost. My goal is a stable leaf yield rather than chasing the highest possible output.
